content.value_statement: Teams need accurate Neon setup guidance across drivers, APIs, and local workflows. This skill directs Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to official Neon references.
actual_capabilities: Explains Neon architecture, autoscaling, branching, instant restore, and scale-to-zero concepts.
Guides project setup, connection strings, dependencies, and schema planning for Neon databases.
Helps choose Neon connection methods for runtimes, drivers, ORMs, and serverless environments.
Directs assistants to Neon documentation through the llms.txt index and official docs pages.
Covers Neon Auth, the Neon JS SDK, Platform API, Neon CLI, TypeScript SDK, and Python SDK.
limitations: Requires current Neon documentation for exact product behavior and API details.
May need network access when an assistant fetches official documentation pages.
Does not create, migrate, or administer Neon resources without separate user-approved tools.
Does not replace secure handling of database credentials, tokens, and production access policies.

prompt_templates.title: Understand Neon Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Neon Serverless Postgres for a developer new to the platform. Include key concepts and when each feature matters.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through setting up a Neon database for my application. Cover connection strings, dependencies, schema setup, and local development.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Connection Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend the best Neon connection approach for my runtime, framework, ORM, and deployment target. Explain tradeoffs and required packages.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Neon workflow using branching, the Platform API, CLI automation, and secure credential handling for a CI/CD environment.

output_examples.input: I need a Neon setup plan for a new web app.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan covering project creation, connection choice, environment variables, schema setup, and documentation links to verify current details.

output_examples.input: Which Neon driver should I use for an edge function?
output_examples.output: A recommendation that compares serverless HTTP, WebSocket, ORM support, pooling needs, and runtime limits before choosing an approach.

output_examples.input: Help document Neon branching for my team.
output_examples.output: A concise operations guide explaining branch purpose, restore workflows, CLI or API options, and credential safety expectations.

best_practices: Verify product details against official Neon documentation before giving final guidance.
Choose connection methods based on runtime limits, pooling needs, latency, and ORM compatibility.
Keep database credentials out of prompts, logs, examples, and shared documentation.
anti_patterns: Do not guess Neon documentation URLs when the docs index can confirm the right page.
Do not recommend one driver for every runtime without checking platform constraints.
Do not include real connection strings or API tokens in examples or troubleshooting output.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps assistants answer Neon Serverless Postgres questions using structured guidance and official documentation references.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it choose a Neon driver or ORM?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides connection method decisions across drivers, ORMs, runtimes, and serverless environments.

faq.question: Does it manage my Neon account directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and references, but direct account changes require separate tools and user approval.

faq.question: Why does it mention curl?
faq.answer: The skill shows optional curl examples for fetching public Neon documentation as Markdown.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Do not place real database URLs, passwords, or API keys in prompts, examples, logs, or generated documentation.
